header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Time: 15:30 UTC (58 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jules Ramirez (Redwood CSM), Daniel Reyes (CTO, Ironwood), Samantha Cho (Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (DevOps), Priya Mehta (Security)
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion sync: Ironwood considering 12-month contract extension with +30% committed capacity, add EU regions (Frankfurt, Ireland), and pilot on-prem private deployment for data residency. Discussed latency targets, burst pricing, operational runbook, security requirements. Agreed next steps: bench, quote, SOC2 addendum, schedule pilot kickoff.
topics: Agenda: 1) current usage and forecast 2) region requirements 3) private deployment pilot 4) SLA and security 5) pricing and contract changes 6) next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Nina Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Daniel Reyes: Hey all, Daniel here.
[00:09] Samantha Cho: Sam on my side.
[00:11] Liam O'Connor: Liam, DevOps.
[00:13] Priya Mehta: Priya, security.
[00:15] Marcus Li: Marcus here from Redwood, will handle the bench and tech questions.
[00:20] Jules Ramirez: Jules from CS.
[00:25] Nina: Great, thanks. We're here to go over renewal and the expansion asks you shared — region add and on‑prem pilot. Roughly 45 minutes of discussion and then a short recap. Does that sound right?
[00:36] Daniel: Yes, perfect. We want to make sure latency is solid in EU and that the cost model works with our forecasting.
[00:44] Nina: Cool. Marcus, do you want to open with current performance notes?
[00:48] Marcus: Sure. From what we've seen, Ironwood's current fleet — you're on a mix of hosted and dedicated nodes, right? The tail latencies at peak are around 240–300ms for your chat flows with 512 token windows. There's room to tune batching and your prefix cache to bring that down to under 200 at scale.
[01:05] Liam: Yeah we've noticed some spikes during nightly batch jobs, maybe due to large context loads.
[01:11] Marcus: That tracks, the KV cache warmup and longer sequences can cause jitter. For the EU regions you mentioned, we can provision geo‑proxied endpoints and reserve dedicated capacity. The question is whether you want dedicated pools in EU (Frankfurt + Ireland) or to start with edge routing to hosted EU nodes.
[01:32] Samantha: Prefer dedicated in EU if we commit, because of data flow and compliance. Our infra team wants predictable throughput.
[01:38] Daniel: Agreed. Cost is a concern, but predictable is more important than slightly cheaper burst.
[01:44] Nina: Understood. On the contract side, a 12‑month extension with a 30% uplift in committed capacity is the usual ask — we can include burst capacity at a defined premium and caps. We'll put that in the draft.
[01:55] Daniel: Also, for the on‑prem pilot — it's for sensitive models and PII handling. We want to test private deployment in our Frankfurt colo. Will the private control plane connect to your console? How much is the management overhead?
[02:12] Marcus: Good Q. For Private, the control plane is customer‑managed (you run the VPC connectors and we provide an ops agent and the artifacts). There's an on‑prem package that installs the runtime; telemetry can be forwarded or held locally per your policy. There is some setup work — standard: networking, KMS integration, and image deployment. We estimate 3–4 weeks for pilot if we get access to the colo environment early.
[02:37] Priya: From security lens — we need to see your SOC 2 plus the KMS/HSM integration doc, and we need to confirm logs aren't sent to third parties. Can we get a non‑production deployment with logs disabled?
[02:49] Jules: Yes, we can provide a security packet and an option to keep logs local. We'll attach the SOC 2 addendum and a KMS integration guide.
[02:56] Nina: I'll also attach the private deployment runbook.
[02:59] Samantha: For EU latency SLOs we want 95th <= 150ms for interactive flows. Is that achievable with dedicated smaller sequence length?
[03:09] Marcus: With dedicated pools in region and tuned batching, 95th of 150ms is aggressive but feasible for token sizes up to ~256, assuming autoscaling headroom and cache warm. For 512 tokens, it'll be tougher without more capacity. We'll run a realistic bench to validate.
[03:25] Liam: Any special kernel/quant settings we should use for the bench?
[03:28] Marcus: We'll use the same quant profile you're using in prod — 4bit quant and the performance kernels. If you want to test 8k context modes that's a different path.
[03:36] Daniel: Not now, just standard production model.
[03:38] Nina: Okay. Let's talk pricing: tiered committed capacity plus burst. We can add a monthly reservation with overage at discounted rate and a burst bucket charged per token. Typical structure: base commit X, burst up to Y hours per month at 50% premium, and emergency spare at 2x.
[03:55] Samantha: Can you do a 6‑month ramp schedule in the contract? We prefer staggered increases.
[03:59] Nina: Yes, staggered ramp is fine. We'll model a three‑step uplift (10% at month 1, +10% at month 4, final +10% at month 8).
[04:10] Daniel: Are there penalties for exceeding commit? We want flexibility.
[04:13] Nina: No hard penalties; it's overage billing. The only penalty comes if you reduce committed capacity mid‑term — that's subject to amendment.
[04:20] Marcus: Quick tech note: for throughput scaling we recommend horizontal pools instead of single giant instance to keep KV cache locality.
[04:27] Liam: Makes sense.
[04:29] [06:05] Samantha: A couple of ops questions — what does the provisioning window look like for EU dedicated nodes?
[06:09] Nina: Once contract signed and payment cleared, we can provision in ~10 business days for standard SKUs; for reserved GPUs or specific instance types it could be 2–3 weeks. For private on‑prem install it's ~3–4 weeks as Marcus mentioned.
[06:24] Daniel: We need SLA language on latency and availability. Can you include a 99.95% availability objective and credit structure?
[06:32] Jules: We can propose SLA credits similar to industry standard; we'll include an availability SLO and a latency SLO for the committed pools.
[06:40] Priya: Also, on audit logs — we need an exportable audit trail for 12 months and integration with our SIEM.
[06:46] Marcus: We support export to S3 and direct SIEM syslog/ELK forwards for Private. For hosted we can provide an S3 export and log retention tiers.
[06:55] Priya: Good.
[06:57] [12:00] Daniel: On migration — our plan is to shift EU traffic gradually over a month. We'd like canary routing and auto‑fallback back to global region if a node is degraded. How does Redwood handle fallbacks?
[12:12] Marcus: We have smart routing rules: you can define priority lists, latency thresholds, and automatic fallback to next region or model variant. Canary is supported via rollout policies in the console — you can route x% of traffic to EU pool and monitor.
[12:25] Samantha: Great. We also need to be careful about data egress for models — ensuring model weights don't leave our controlled environment for Private.
[12:33] Marcus: For Private the weights and runtime stay on your infra. For Dedicated/Hosted, model artifacts are in our managed storage; we can employ encryption at rest and regional isolation.
[12:45] [18:00] Daniel: On cost estimates — can you give rough numbers for a 30% uplift? We need an internal CAPEX/OPEX comparison for private pilot vs reserved cloud.
[18:12] Nina: We'll produce a side‑by‑side estimate: committed reserved cost, burst charges, and private deployment one‑time setup fee plus monthly support/license. Expect private pilot to have higher setup but potentially lower per‑token cost long term depending on utilization.
[18:27] Samantha: Put the spreadsheet in the shared folder with line items.
[18:30] Nina: Will do, I'll attach the pricing spreadsheet.
[18:33] [23:00] Liam: Bench specifics — we care most about p50, p95, p99 for 256 tokens and 512 tokens. Also throughput at 1000 concurrent QPS for our peak sim.
[23:10] Marcus: We'll run both sizes and synthetic and a replay using a subset of your prod prompt patterns (need sample prompts). We'll also run KV cache warm and cold tests.
[23:20] Daniel: I'll share an anonymized prompt set post call.
[23:23] Nina: Thanks.
[23:25] [28:00] Priya: A couple of legal/security items: we need to add a data processing addendum for EU customers, standard breach notification timings, and a KMS rotation policy.
[28:10] Jules: We'll include the DPA and a rotation policy. For breach notifications the standard 72 hours is workable and we'll document escalation paths.
[28:20] Priya: Also we've had internal audits asking for RBAC and SSO options — can Redwood integrate with our Okta instance?
[28:27] Marcus: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta is supported; RBAC can be mapped to teams. For Private, you can enforce SSO locally.
[28:36] [34:00] Samantha: One operational nit — what observability will our app team see? Token‑level cost, per‑route latency?
[34:07] Jules: The Console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces and error logs. We can provision a limited access view for your app team.
[34:18] Samantha: Perfect.
[34:20] [40:00] Daniel: Can we talk about rollback path for model regressions? If we push an updated model and quality drops, how fast can we roll back?
[40:09] Marcus: Rollback is immediate if you pin previous model versions. We also support canary traffic and automated regression alerts tied to prompt sets if you want a guardrail.
[40:19] Daniel: Ok, we'll want auto rollback on critical regression thresholds.
[40:23] Nina: We'll include suggested thresholds in the playbook.
[40:26] [46:00] Samantha: On billing and invoicing: Ironwood prefers monthly invoices with usage reconciliation. Can Redwood provide detailed usage exports?
[46:09] Jules: Yes, CSV exports and API access for granular token and route usage. We'll agree on billing cadence in the quote.
[46:20] Daniel: One last ask — can you include migration assistance as part of the renewal for EU onramp, maybe a small number of professional services hours?
[46:31] Nina: We can include a 40‑hour onboarding credit for migration in the renewal bundle.
[46:36] Daniel: That would help sell it internally.
[46:38] Nina: Great. We are at about 50 minutes, any final questions?
[46:45] Priya: Please make sure the SOC 2 docs include the scope of production vs nonprod.
[46:51] Jules: We'll mark that clearly.
[46:54] [56:00] Nina: Okay recap — action items: Marcus to run bench (due 5/15), Nina to send draft amendment + quote (due 5/12), Jules to send onboarding playbook and pricing spreadsheet (due 5/14), Priya to send SOC2 and questions (due 5/11). We'll schedule the pilot kickoff week of 5/25 pending readiness. Anything to add?
[56:22] Daniel: No that's it, sounds good.
[56:25] Samantha: Thanks everyone.
[56:28] Nina: Thanks all, we will follow up via email with the attachments and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[56:35] [58:00] End of recording.
